summary.intent: Land Rust language support in monokl (an analyzer plus a Rust eval harness) through a parallel agent workflow with adversarial review. Then, prompted by the issues found, make performance a first-class architectural concern.
summary.outcome: PR #76 (Rust eval, CI green) and PR #77 (Rust analyzer, review findings fixed, CI pending) are ready for merge. Two measurement-first agents were launched, an architecture risk review and a `just bench` harness, to inform a performance ADR; bench files were added or modified.

repo: Rust analysis uses ra_ap_syntax pinned at 0.0.349 behind the default-on `lang-rust` feature; 0.0.350+ needs Rust 1.98 while the MSRV is 1.96, so the pin must be bumped when the MSRV moves.
Test code (#[cfg(test)], #[test], etc.) goes to a separate FileAnalysis.test_blocks field and is included only with --tests. This avoided changing CodeBlock's 34 construction sites.
ra_ap_syntax drops trees on a shared 2 MiB thread, so deep trees overflow and abort the process. Trees deeper than 2000 (debug) or 8000 (release) are leaked and the file is degraded as TooDeep.
The ra parser is quadratic in nesting depth: 260 KB of pure nesting takes minutes, so a hostile file could stall a search.

The parse-stack cap was raised from 1 GiB to 4 GiB to read files up to about 1 MB. It is shared with TypeScript, so every parse thread reserves 4 GiB of address space, which may fail under container or ulimit -v limits.

scripts/rg-compare.py is now language-aware via an optional 4th column in rg-compare.repos (ts default, rust), with Rust results pooled under --min-rust-recall (default 0). The Rust baseline was 0/24 before the analyzer; the TS gates are unchanged (98.31% / 94.44% / 93.75%).

Trait method parents render as `interface Foo` because the shared SymbolKind has no Trait variant. The 'only top-level declarations and members of classes and objects' hint in output/agent.rs is TS-worded.

Review fixes: test methods inside non-test impl/trait now own their hits; tests.rs, test.rs, *_tests.rs and *_test.rs count as test paths; macro invocations and extern blocks become blocks; a missing analyzer gives a Skipped diagnostic.
Known performance observations: dedup of ~1,678 candidate blocks took ~30 ms, tokenizer vocabulary load cost ~50 ms per matching search, and each invocation re-parses matching files from scratch.
workflow: A parallel dynamic workflow of implementer, eval, adversarial reviewer and fixer agents surfaced real high-severity bugs that the implementer's own tests missed. The review reproduced each against concrete inputs.
Agent-reported CI results should be verified independently: the lead checked PR CI status itself, and #77's Linux CI is the first real test of the stack-size concern.

Performance work is done measurement-first: a read-only risk review and a benchmark script run before any product code changes, then decisions go in an ADR, with one small PR per violated item ordered by payoff.
Timings on a heavily loaded machine (load average ~25) were noisy, so benchmark comparisons need interleaved medians and shouldn't gate on a single run.

friction: The machine was heavily loaded during the agents' runs, making timing numbers noisy and the Rust search timing inconclusive.
The agent did not test Linux, so the 4 GiB stack reservation risk is unverified.
The ra_ap_syntax version pin was forced by the MSRV mismatch with 0.0.350+.
One-at-a-time fixing of performance issues found them without producing a general design rule.
open_items: Verify #77's Linux CI and test the 4 GiB stack reservation under constrained container or ulimit -v limits before merging.
Decide on a nesting-depth pre-check or parse timeout to bound ra_ap_syntax's quadratic behavior on hostile files.
After #77 passes CI, rerun the Rust eval and raise --min-rust-recall to the measured level.

Write a performance-architecture ADR from the risk review and bench results (candidates: two-phase search, on-disk analysis cache, long-lived session, or stateless with hard bounds), then open one small PR per violated item.
Build the held-out question set to address tuning risk, and run it on the settled design.
Run the speed comparison of #74 and #75 combined against rg.
Add a Trait SymbolKind or Rust-specific label in the output layer, and fix the TS-worded hint in output/agent.rs.

Low-severity items left unfixed: duplicated snippet signature for name-only matches on attributed functions, edition-2015 code parsed as current edition, weak presence-style test assertions, and one CLI test failing in a Rust-only build.
Merge order pending user approval: #76, then #77, plus #74 and #75; Entire Gates on each await approval.
